1.explanation: In lib/emulation.js the function enableNexus5X explicitly calls Network.setUserAgentOverride with the Nexus 5X UA, so the actual HTTP requests use that mobile UA. However in gather/driver.js the method getUserAgent (used to populate artifacts.UserAgent and subsequently lhr.userAgent/runtimeSettings.userAgent) still returns the browser’s default UA (e.g. the CrOS UA) because it never queries or reflects the override. To fix the mismatch, getUserAgent must be updated to return the overridden UA (for example by reading back the value passed to Network.setUserAgentOverride or via a CDP Network.getUserAgentOverride call), so that the report’s displayed UA matches the actual header sent.
1.bug_scenario: When you run Lighthouse in mobile emulation (for example “Emulated Nexus 5X”), the network requests sent by Chrome actually carry the mobile User-Agent string defined in emulation.js (the Android/Nexus UA), but the Lighthouse report’s “Runtime settings → User agent” line is still showing the original desktop CrOS UA. In other words, network logs show one UA (the override), while the report header shows another (the default).

2.explanation:
• In lib/emulation.js the constant NEXUS5X_USERAGENT and function enableNexus5X are responsible for telling Chrome DevTools to override the network UA header when emulating a Nexus 5X. That part is working correctly, so your server sees the Mobile UA.  
• However, in gather/driver.js the Driver.getUserAgent method (called during artifact collection) is still using the browser’s original UA (via the un-implemented stub that never picks up the override), and Driver.beginEmulation doesn’t update how getUserAgent behaves after the override.  
• Because the report prints runtimeSettings.userAgent based on Driver.getUserAgent (not on the active Network.setUserAgentOverride), the report shows the wrong UA string.  
To fix this you need to have Driver.getUserAgent return the same UA string that emulation.js passes to Network.setUserAgentOverride (or to read it back from the DevTools protocol), and ensure beginEmulation wires up that override before getUserAgent is called.
2.bug_scenario: When Lighthouse runs in mobile emulation (for example, Nexus 5X) it correctly overrides the network‐level User-Agent header (so your server sees the Mobile UA), but the “Runtime settings → User agent” string printed in the HTML report still shows the browser’s original desktop UA. In the screenshots you can see two different UAs (the emulated Mobile UA in the access.log vs. the CrOS/Linux UA in the report), which is confusing and incorrect — the report should reflect the actual UA override used on the network.
